newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cabinet demands apology from Havel.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cabinet demands apology from Havel.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesday demanded a public apology from Czech President Vaclav Havel for his remarks to a French newspaper about Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.

"We consider the remarks by President Havel concerning Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar to the French daily Le Figaro as a gross violation of the basic tenets of decency in the communication between representatives of two sovereign and equal republics," said a statement issued in the name of all members of the cabinet.
Last week Meciar scrapped his first official visit to Prague, scheduled for later this month, because of Czech criticism of Bratislava.
According to Slovak media reports Havel suggested that Meciar was "paranoid" in the Figaro interview.
Havel and his office have refused to comment on these reports after requests by local media.
The context of the remarks was that Meciar was overly sensitive to Czech criticism of Slovakia.

"We consider insults and the lack of esteem for the Slovak prime minister from the lips of the highest representative of a neighbouring state not only as inappropriate interference into the internal affairs of Slovakia but as damaging the Slovak Republic and one of its highest representatives in the eyes of the European and world public," the Slovak ministers said.

The latest statement followed similar Slovak comments last week attacking Czech press and public statements on Slovakia and a critical Slovak foreign ministry statement, highlighted the chill between the former partners in the Czechoslovak federation.

The Czechs and Slovaks have yet to settle numerous issues arising from their peaceful 1993 split of Czechoslovakia -- dubbed the "Velvet Divorce" -- such as the divsion of federal gold reserves and cultural artifacts, and cross ownership of some banks.

The Czech National Bank has said the federation's gold reserves were split two-to-one in Prague's favour, roughly the same ratio as the two populations as a whole, but the Slovaks claim Prague still holds a large amount of Slovak gold.
The main purpose of Meciar's planned visit was to sign final agreements on the division of property of the former federation.
